## Overview

Containers are becoming increasingly popular in bioinformatics as we move into an
era of heightened emphasis on reproducible research.

Containers are pieces of software that bundle an operating system and all of the
dependencies your program needs to run — there is no need to install anything but
a container platform, such as Docker or Singularity. What makes this even better
is that containers are stable over time, so you can share them with future-you or
with collaborators anywhere in the world, and it will be as if you are running the
same system.

What are the finer details surrounding containers? What are they used for? Where
can you get them? What can you do with them? These are the questions we answer in
this session.

## Prerequisites

No preparation reading necessary — just come and learn about containers with us.
